newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PALACE AND SHEFFIELD TO VIE FOR PREMIER LEAGUE SPOT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PALACE AND SHEFFIELD TO VIE FOR PREMIER LEAGUE SPOT.

text.p: Crystal Palace earned a place in the English first division playoffs for the second successive year when they held off a determined challenge by Wolverhampton on Wednesday.
The London club will meet Sheffield United, winners on the away goals rule over Ipswich, at Wembley on May 26 for a place in the premier league.
The match at Ipswich ended 2-2 after extra time following a 1-1 draw in the first leg last weekend.
Wolves won 2-1 on the night but Palace took the two-leg playoff by dint of their 3-1 victory in the first leg.

Palace, beaten in last season's playoff final by Leicester, faced a frantic last five minutes after Adrian Williams headed Wolves into a 2-1 lead. But although Wolves continually swarmed forward the Palace defence held out.
Wolves had given themselves every chance of reeling in Palace's first leg advantage when Mark Atkins put them ahead with almost an hour of the match left.
But that chance effectively ended when David Hopkin burst through the centre of the field to drive home a left-foot shot soon after the interval.
Andy Walker scored the vital goal which earned Sheffield United their chance of premier soccer next season.
Belarus international Petr Katchouro had put United ahead in the ninth minute but James Scowcroft levelled for Ipswich in the 32nd minute.

Ipswich looked to heading for Wembley when Swedish international Niklas Gudmundsson put them 2-1 ahead in the 73rd minute but then Scotland international Walker scored the equaliser with 13 minutes remaining.
Ipswich went all out for the winner in extra time but United hung on despite having Nick Henry sent off in the 110th minute for his second bookable offence.
